symptom: After the server's `config.json` was set to `127.0.0.1:9222`, the next code sync put the laptop's browser address back: the selftest silently skipped the modal check, and the pipeline on the server would have gone blind on the first poll.
cause: `config.json` sits next to the code and contains the browser address, a machine-specific setting in a file synced as code. `.env` and `state/` were excluded from the sync; it was not.
rule: While both machines are alive, sync code only with `--exclude config.json --exclude state/ --exclude .env`; after retiring the laptop, set the repository's `config.json` to the server values so the exclusion becomes unnecessary. The reverse side: after the migration the server writes the artifacts (ledgers), so before pushing code pull those directories first. Check after every sync with the selftest: 'Chrome unreachable over CDP' means exactly a drifted address.

title: Size the VPS from measured PSS at peak, not from the cheapest plan
symptom: The migration budget had been set to the cheapest VPS tier, i.e. 1 vCPU and 1-2 GB RAM.
cause: The plan was chosen by price, not by the load profile. The pipeline keeps a headful Chrome running and launches up to two headless model CLI calls in a row.
rule: Measure PSS before renting and size for the peak, not the average. Measured: Chrome with two tabs 1.0 GB PSS (28 processes), each headless CLI call 230-520 MB, pipeline peak about 2.2 GB, so a minimum of 2 vCPU / 4 GB. On the cheapest tier the OOM kill would land exactly at submission time, the one minute everything is built for.

title: SPA buttons under CDP: el.click() and keyboard first, real mouse last
symptom: Real mouse clicks (`mouse.click`) on the SPA's buttons worked only sometimes; `Save & Continue` in an editor did not post to the server (step data lost on URL change), and dialogs hung after Save.
cause: Some buttons and dropdowns of the component library do not react to the synthetic CDP mouse stream; plus silent client-side validation (a required category field) with no error message.
rule: (1) First JS `el.click()` and keyboard (focus + Enter for dropdowns), mouse last; (2) for editor steps call the Vue component method directly (`vm.next()`, `vm.sendToReview()`, found via `__vue__` on the button's ancestors) and verify the POST and the URL change; (3) re-read the page after every step, never trust 'clicked'.

title: Backspace in an empty tag input deletes the previous tag
symptom: When adding skills through a typeahead, after each new tag only that one tag remained.
cause: Clearing the field with Ctrl+A, Backspace on an empty input removes the last tag: standard tag-input behaviour.
rule: Clear only when the value is non-empty and use Delete; after each addition re-read the list of tags.

title: The ffmpeg shipped in the Playwright cache cannot encode GIF
symptom: `ffmpeg-linux` from `~/.cache/ms-playwright/ffmpeg-*` fails on `palettegen` / the GIF encoder when building demo GIFs.
cause: It is a stripped build meant only for Playwright's webm recording.
rule: Use a full `ffmpeg-static` build for GIF (pass it via an env variable) or assemble frames with PIL; do not spend time debugging the filters.

title: pkill -f <string> kills the agent's own Bash tool shell
symptom: A command containing `pkill -f "...server.js"` exits with code 144 and the rest of the chain never runs.
cause: The pattern matches the command line of the tool's own shell, which contains the same text.
rule: Kill background processes by port (`fuser -k 8787/tcp`) or by PID file; do not use `pkill -f`.

title: Windows interop directories are missing from the Bash tool's PATH
symptom: The bridge script fails with `powershell.exe: command not found` even with the sandbox disabled.
cause: The tool shell's PATH lacks `/mnt/c/Windows/System32[/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0]`.
rule: Before any bridge or notification scripts run `export PATH="$PATH:/mnt/c/Windows/System32:/mnt/c/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0"` (baked into the run script).

title: `claude -p --bare` loses the login; use `--setting-sources ""` instead
symptom: A proxy over the CLI answered `Not logged in`; without the flag it answered in Russian because the global CLAUDE.md says 'always reply in Russian'.
cause: `--bare` skips reading the keychain/credentials; CLAUDE.md is mixed into any `-p` call.
rule: For programmatic `claude -p` calls use `--setting-sources ""` plus an explicit `--system-prompt`, without `--bare`; remove `CLAUDECODE` from the environment (nested call).

title: A Quill editor drops non-ASCII and jumps the caret; insert via insertText
symptom: After typing a description the text came out shuffled in chunks; characters like em dash, bullet, arrow, curly quotes and check marks disappeared; when typing from the keyboard the caret jumped to the start after such a character.
cause: The editor's fields (Quill description, inputs) filter non-ASCII on input; removing a character resets the selection.
rule: Normalize all texts for that editor to ASCII before input (bullet to `-`, arrow to `->`, em dash to `-`, straight quotes); insert the description paragraph by paragraph with `execCommand('insertText')` plus Enter and verify paragraphs via `.ql-editor p`, not `innerText` (Quill doubles line breaks in `innerText`).

title: Class-component popovers and react-select ignore CDP clicks; use fiber state
symptom: Clicking `CHOOSE...` / `SELECT A CATEGORY` did not open the list; searching options by text hit footer links with the same text.
cause: The site's Popover is a class component rendered with `appendToBody`: the container with `<button value=...>` is already in the DOM and opening happens through state; react-select renders options as `[id*="-option-"]` in a portal.
rule: For Popover/Select walk up `__reactFiber` to the stateNode with `open()`/`state.isOpen`, call `open()`, then click the `<button>` inside `state.container` by text or value; search for elements by text only inside the relevant block.

title: React re-renders fields after input; old handles type into detached nodes
symptom: Of three package name fields only one got filled and a price stayed empty; `typeInto` reported success but the values were missing.
cause: After the first input React recreates the textarea/input elements; handles collected in advance point to detached nodes.
rule: Take the handle again right before typing into each field and read the value back afterwards; loop 'fill, verify, repeat the missing ones'.

title: A native confirm() without a dialog handler freezes the tab for CDP
symptom: After clicking a bulk DELETE every CDP command to the tab hung (even `Page.enable`), `puppeteer.connect` did not answer, and `No dialog is showing` appeared after killing the process.
cause: `confirm('Are you sure you want to delete...')` blocks the renderer; without `page.on('dialog')` nobody closes it.
rule: Attach `page.on('dialog')` before the click in any such script; cure a frozen tab with browser-level `Target.closeTarget` plus `Target.createTarget`, not by restarting the bridge. The deletion has no further confirmation in the UI, so take a backup beforehand.

title: spawnSync with encoding:'utf8' corrupts multibyte characters on chunk boundaries
symptom: A draft and a chat header contained a Cyrillic word with a replacement character in the middle, while the JSON from the child CLI was valid.
cause: `spawnSync` with `encoding` decodes the stream in chunks; a multibyte UTF-8 character that falls on a buffer boundary is corrupted.
rule: Launch child processes without `encoding` and decode the whole buffer at once: `(r.stdout || Buffer.alloc(0)).toString('utf8')`. Applies to every wrapper around child scripts.

title: Headless `claude -p`: no --bare, cwd outside the repo, per-model fallback chain
symptom: `claude -p --bare ...` answered `Not logged in · Please run /login` despite a working login; later `You've reached your ... limit` for one model stopped the automation mid-run.
cause: `--bare` skips loading the settings where the subscription's OAuth session lives; the limit is counted per model.
rule: For headless calls use `claude -p --no-session-persistence --output-format json --json-schema ...` without `--bare`, with `cwd` outside the repo (so the project CLAUDE.md is not pulled in) and with the nested session's `CLAUDE*` variables cleared; set the model explicitly and keep a fallback chain (`sonnet` to `opus` to `haiku`), switching on the error text (`limit|overloaded|429|quota`).

title: A stop script's cleanup outside the per-daemon branch killed the other daemon
symptom: `stop.sh listener` also stopped the monitor, which silently stopped polling.
cause: At the end of the script a 'leftover' cleanup via `pkill -f monitor.js` and `pkill -f tg-listener.js` sat outside the loop over the selected daemon and always ran.
rule: In daemon control scripts every operation (kill, pkill, PID-file removal) lives inside the branch of the specific daemon; after editing, verify that stopping one does not touch the other (`ps` before and after).

title: Custom currency input and dropdown: keyboard only; textarea via native setter
symptom: A currency input showed `$0.00` after a JS setter; a dropdown option was not selected by JS click or synthetic mouse events on the LI; the toggle stayed at `Select a duration`.
cause: The currency component formats its value on keyup/blur and ignores programmatic input; the dropdown listens to keyboard and real mouse.
rule: Amount: `focus + select`, Ctrl+A, `keyboard.type`, Tab. Dropdown: focus the toggle, Enter, ArrowDown until `[role=option].is-focused` has the wanted text, Enter. Textareas: native setter plus input/change events. Always read the values back.

title: A custom dropdown: mouse opens but does not select; track document.activeElement
symptom: A form would have gone out without a duration: `Select a duration` and `Value is required and can't be empty` although the script reported 'form filled'.
cause: Three layers: (1) options render in a portal outside the toggle's container, and `[role=option]` elements of the site's header search sit in the DOM at the same time, so 'first option' missed; (2) a mouse click on `li[role=option]` closes the list without changing the value, only the keyboard selects; (3) the earlier marker `[role=option].is-focused` is not set by this component; track `document.activeElement` instead. Also, with a value already selected the list opens on it, and ArrowDown does not wrap at the end.
rule: Open the list with a real mouse click at coordinates, assert `aria-expanded=true`, read the visible options (`getBoundingClientRect().height > 0`), compute the indexes of the current and target options, move with ArrowUp/ArrowDown by index confirming each step via `document.activeElement`, then Enter and compare the toggle text. Replaces the earlier 'Enter from focus + ArrowDown until .is-focused' method. General rule: every form-filling script ends with a self-check of the fields and returns an explicit list of problems; a silent 'done' is worse than an honest error.

title: Pre-send checks must read the form back, not the draft file
symptom: The draft in the file was perfect while the form held something else: the amount did not land in the currency input, the duration stayed unselected, the cover letter went into the wrong textarea, a screening answer was empty. A file-based check passed all of it and allowed the send.
cause: Between the draft and the submit button lies a prefill layer that can fail silently (custom components, portals, tab focus). The file is the intent, the form is the fact.
rule: Any automatic pre-send check reads the form (`--readback`) and compares every field with the draft: amount, duration, mode, cover letter, each answer by index. A reviewing model also gets the text from the form, not the file. Take the cost from the submit button itself and compare it with the expected cost, otherwise an add-on can be sent silently.

title: The submit button may not be the last click: a confirmation modal follows
symptom: The auto-submit clicked the send button, waited 60 s, re-checked the form in a separate tab and honestly reported 'not sent: the form still asks for credits'. Every attempt went like this; manual sends from the same tab worked.
cause: On fixed-price items the site opens a `3 things you need to know` disclaimer after the click, with a checkbox and a Continue button disabled until it is ticked. Until the modal is passed nothing is sent and the form stays put, looking exactly like a failed send. A human passes it without thinking and never mentions it.
rule: After the 'final' click in a foreign UI do not judge the outcome until you have checked for a confirmation step. While waiting, look for the modal on every turn and pass it (checkbox then Continue), pressing the final button once. The checkbox is drawn as a sprite (`input` 1x1): click the visible label with the mouse, with `el.click()` as a fallback. Test on a fixture with the same markup, because a live test costs a submission.

title: Parsing child output as 'first { to last }' breaks on a trailing line
symptom: The auto-submit reported 'the prefill tool did not answer' and sent 'send failed, credits intact', although the child process had finished and returned normal JSON with the outcome.
cause: The child's output was parsed by slicing from the first `{` to the last `}`. In `--send` mode the tool prints one more line `SEND: {...}` after the JSON block, so the slice captured both objects and stopped parsing. That branch was the only one with such a tail and the only one never run on real output.
rule: Test a child-output parser on the real output of every mode, not only the main one; parse not 'first brace to last brace' but walk `}` from the end to the first valid JSON. And a false 'did not work' on an action that already happened in the world is more dangerous than an honest error: it breaks act-then-log and invites a repeat.

title: pkill -f on a path pattern kills the supervisor loop and the calling shell
symptom: `pkill -f "node .*tg-listener.js"` meant to restart a daemon also killed its supervisor loop (same path in its command line) and the calling command (exit 144). The listener stayed down unattended until noticed.
cause: `-f` compares the pattern with the full command line of any process, including `bash -c "while true; do node ..."` and the current shell.
rule: Restart daemons under a supervisor loop with their own tools (`stop.sh`, `run.sh <name>`, idempotent), not `pkill`. For a targeted kill use only the PID of the process itself (`ps aux`), never a path pattern. After any restart check `ps` and the log tail: a live supervisor without a node process looks almost like a working pipeline.

title: Tab cleanup keyed on the pre-action ID finds nothing once the URL changes
symptom: After every send the log said `tabs closed 0`, and confirmation tabs piled up in the browser (three in two days) although cleanup ran and raised no errors.
cause: `closeJobTabs` looked for tabs by the item ID in the URL, but a successful send navigates to `/proposals/<proposalId>?success`, a different identifier from a different namespace. Zero closed tabs read as 'nothing to close' rather than 'not found'.
rule: If an action changes the tab's URL, cleanup cannot rely on the 'before' identifier alone: remember the 'after' identifier (it is in the outcome confirmation) or close by the result-page signature. A `done 0` counter in a log is not proof of success; for cleanup log what was searched for and what was found.

title: tls.connect(port, host, cb) sends no SNI; Gmail's default cert looks like MITM
symptom: An IMAP login check from the server failed with `ERR self-signed certificate` connecting to `imap.gmail.com:993`. On a rented datacenter machine that reads as TLS interception, right when an app password was about to be sent there.
cause: The positional form `tls.connect(993, 'imap.gmail.com', cb)` does not pass `servername`, so no SNI is sent. Without SNI Gmail serves a default certificate whose chain does not verify. No interception: `openssl s_client -connect imap.gmail.com:993 -servername imap.gmail.com` showed the real chain and `Verify return code: 0 (ok)`.
rule: Write TLS clients only in the object form: `tls.connect({ host, port, servername })`. Before declaring 'we are being intercepted', verify the chain with an independent tool: a certificate error far more often means a bug in your own code than an attack.

title: A placeholder from an instruction lands in .env verbatim and silently
symptom: The server's `.env` contained `INBOX_IMAP_USER=NEW_MAILBOX@gmail.com`: the human had copied the line from the instruction together with the placeholder. The password next to it was real, the file looked filled, `grep -c` showed two lines, the task was marked done.
cause: The instruction asked to paste a command with a placeholder inside, and the check was 'are the keys in the file', not 'do they work'.
rule: A credential line counts as done only after a live login from that machine (IMAP `LOGIN`, an API request, `ssh -T`). Verify by fact, not by presence of the key. In instructions write placeholders in angle brackets and Latin letters (`<APP_PASSWORD>`) so a verbatim paste stands out.

title: A synthetic .click() on Gmail's Send button sends nothing and leaves no trace
symptom: Two canary emails were 'sent' over CDP: `element.click()` on the element labelled Send ran without errors and the script reported `clicked`. The messages were in neither Inbox, Sent nor Drafts; a search with `in:anywhere` found nothing.
cause: Gmail's button is a `div[role=button]` that reacts to a real sequence of mouse events; a programmatic `.click()` never reaches its handler. There is no rollback: the composition lived in the page and the next navigation destroyed it with the text.
rule: For buttons that act on the world (send, publish, pay) click only with a real CDP click on the element from a snapshot, the same way `fill` that does not stick is replaced by `type_text` for inputs. Confirm by the state of the world (a `Message sent` toast, the message visible in a folder), not by the call not throwing.

title: Renaming inside the Windows Startup folder does not disable autostart
symptom: At every Windows login a dialog `Select an app to open this .disabled-2026-08-22 file` appeared with a list of applications. The local pipeline had been considered disarmed since the migration, and no monitor processes existed on the machine.
cause: Autostart was disabled by renaming the `.vbs` to `.vbs.disabled-<date>` while leaving it in the Startup folder. At login Windows tries to open everything in that folder regardless of extension; for an unknown extension it shows an app picker instead of running. The script indeed did not run, but the tail stayed visible to the human every day.
rule: Disable autostart by moving the file out of the Startup folder (into the project's archive), not by renaming in place. Apply the same logic to any 'disabled by suffix' in directories the OS scans wholesale: `/etc/cron.d`, `systemd/*/`, `conf.d`. Verify by enumerating all logon sources (both Startup folders, `Run`/`RunOnce` in HKCU and HKLM, `StartupApproved`, `Policies\Explorer\Run`, scheduled tasks with an AtLogon trigger), not only the place you edited.

title: Sparse new Array(n) fixtures vanish under filter; grep every .length consumer
symptom: Four of nine search queries got `"off": true` and the poll went down to five. The regression failed on a neighbouring check: 'one result out of ten means a failed poll' returned true, i.e. a blind poll counted as successful.
cause: Two traps of one shape: 'the list length stopped meaning what it meant'. First, poll health was computed as `okSearches * 2 >= cfg.queries.length`, and after turning off four queries the denominator stayed nine, so every poll would be 'incomplete' forever and the external watchdog would never be pinged. Second, the test fixture `new Array(10)` is a sparse array, and `filter` skips holes, so the count of live queries collapsed to zero and any number of results passed.
rule: When adding an 'off' flag to a collection, grep for `.length` of that collection and decide for each place whether it means the whole list or the live part; in fixtures use `Array.from({length: n}, () => ({}))`, not `new Array(n)`, otherwise any `filter`/`map` in the code under test silently empties the fixture. A rule extracted from source by a test (`new Function` over a `match`) must stay expressible in the same arguments.

title: Config reached the server but nothing changed: the daemon reads it once
symptom: `git push`, sync on the server, `config.json` in the working directory new, HEAD matching, units `active`. The next poll still read all nine queries as if nothing had changed.
cause: `const cfg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(...))` runs once at module load; the monitor is a `--loop` process that lives for days. Only `.env` is re-read (`reloadEnv()` on every poll), which created the false impression that config is picked up by itself.
rule: Consider a config rollout done only after restarting the consumer and seeing live proof in the log (here: a poll listing exactly the new queries). Restart a daemon that holds a lock on a shared resource in the window between cycles (`sleep NNNs` in the log, lock free), and verify the lock expires on its own so a mid-cycle crash does not block the pipeline. Before a rollout answer 'what is re-read by itself and what only at start' instead of assuming.

title: A cancelled MCP wait_for wedges the server; `curl | head` hides curl's exit code
symptom: A `wait_for` (waiting 4 minutes for a human step) went to the background and was stopped with TaskStop; afterwards `evaluate_script` and even `list_pages` hung for 120 s each, although `curl /json/list` on the CDP port answered instantly and the tab sat on the right page. Separately, `if curl ... | head -c 300; then echo UP` printed `ALREADY UP` with the port closed, and the MCP immediately answered `Could not connect`.
cause: The MCP server executes calls sequentially: TaskStop removes the task on the client side, but inside the server the wait keeps running and holds the queue until its own timeout. In a pipeline `if` looks at the exit code of the last command (`head`), not `curl`.
rule: Do not hang a human-step wait on an MCP `wait_for`: poll with short calls or, more reliably, with a plain puppeteer script over CDP that does not depend on the MCP; after a wedged MCP call do not count on that MCP for the rest of the session. Check a port only with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'` compared to `200`.

title: An ssh -L tunnel from WSL binds only WSL loopback; add a second bind on *
symptom: To let the human click a button on the server's Chrome, a noVNC tunnel was needed. The first command with `pkill -f "ssh ... -L 6080"` killed the tool's own shell (exit 144). The tunnel `-L 6080:127.0.0.1:6080` listened only on WSL's 127.0.0.1 and it was unclear whether a Windows browser would reach it; about 65 minutes were spent waiting, and `timeout ... node wait.js; echo exit=$?` in the background always printed 0.
cause: A `pkill -f` pattern matches the `bash -c` of the tool itself. A local ssh forward binds to WSL's loopback by default, and Windows sees WSL ports through localhostForwarding only sometimes. A long human wait is normal, not an error.
rule: Terminate processes by PID from `ss -tlnp`/`pgrep -x`, never `pkill -f <string>`. Bring the noVNC tunnel up in the background with two binds at once (`-L 6080:...` and `-L '*:6081:...'`) and give the human one URL plus a fallback; close by PID afterwards. Wait for the human with a poller that holds no lock (a lock expires in 5 minutes), one factual message per 15 minutes; do not read the exit code of a background command, print the result in words (`MODAL GONE` / `TIMEOUT`).

title: An SPA panel renders a cached list first and updates later; read until stable
symptom: A dry run read a conversation card as `Client: ... 1:50 PM` although our reply `You: ... 4:43 PM` had been in the thread for 18 minutes and was visible as the third message in the same tab; a re-read 4 s later showed the current preview.
cause: The panel draws from a local cache and only then refreshes with the API response. 'Cards appeared' is not 'cards are current': the same trap as lazily loaded labels, but here the cost is a stale dedup key and a signal late by one whole cycle.
rule: Read such lists until they stabilize: after the first non-empty read, re-read every 2 s until two consecutive reads match (not sooner than 6 s, not longer than 25 s) and take the last non-empty read. Test a new parser on a live page where you know in advance what should be last.

title: Probes that write to the database poison the 'after' run; use a fresh seed
symptom: In the run script the 'before the fix' probes (the attacker making herself owner and admin of another project) ran on the same data as the 'after' probes: in the capture the attacker still saw 4 tasks and `UPDATE 1` after the fix, while the text said 2 tasks and `UPDATE 0`. Noticed by a fact-checker comparing every number against the run file, not by the author or editor.
cause: Policies stop new leaks but do not roll back rows already inserted; CI only checked the error texts 'after'.
rule: Writing probes only on a fresh seed (`fresh` before the fix); CI asserts both states (the 'before' leaks must succeed: `UPDATE 1`, `INSERT 0 1`; 'after' must refuse with `UPDATE 0`); every published number comes from one captured run of the final scripts, never 'roughly the same'.

title: Two background loops polling the GitHub API burned the 60 requests/hour limit
symptom: `api.github.com` stopped returning JSON with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`; the previous step's background `until` loop was still running in parallel with the new one.
cause: Without a token the limit is 60 requests per hour per IP; two loops times 3 requests per minute.
rule: Check CI status with one request after the expected run time (2-3 min), polling no more than once a minute; before a new loop kill the old one by PID from `ps -eo pid,args | grep <sha>` (not `pkill -f`); at `remaining: 0` wait for `x-ratelimit-reset` (`date -d @<epoch>`).

title: Timing an RLS policy: JIT and qual order change the number several-fold
symptom: `count(*)` under an EXISTS policy took 441 ms on the first measurement and 19 ms on the third; a per-row `auth.uid()` variant took 133 ms in one run and 17 ms in another for the same query; on a machine where two subagents were working in parallel the JIT section doubled (216 ms vs 125 ms).
cause: The cost estimate of the correlated EXISTS in the policy was 3.2 million (the planner prices the per-row subplan alternative and executes the hashed one), triggering about 125 ms of JIT compilation on every query; in the second case the cheap hash subplan came first in the AND, so `auth.uid()` was evaluated only for surviving rows.
rule: First `explain (analyze, costs on)` and the JIT section, then believe the milliseconds; for policy measurements `set jit = off` explicitly and show the trap separately; measure the expression in the position the claim is about (inside the policy), not in a WHERE next to another policy; take the final run on a quiet machine after the subagents are done.

title: A web-research subagent paraphrases sources and marks its own facts verified
symptom: A weekly staleness check was done by a subagent (19 web calls); its report carried check marks. The facts were copied into the review, the wiki log and the handoff with the caveat 'per the subagent'. Verifying the primary sources before the summary found two errors out of six: two quarterly percentages were wrong by several points, and a changelog claim about existing database tables was inverted (the changelog said existing tables were not affected); the subagent's link led to a 404.
cause: The subagent retells secondary sources and awards itself check marks. Retelling loses caveats (`existing tables are not affected`) and mixes up metrics from neighbouring lines of a report. The 'per the subagent' caveat does not stop the error from entering long-term memory and conclusions.
rule: A fact from a web subagent enters project memory only after the agent itself opened the primary source (press release, changelog, the platform's own help) and checked the quote. Not verified means not written. Demand verbatim quotes with URLs from the subagent, not a retelling. Verify before writing, not before the summary.
